title: A stable implementation of a data-driven scale-aware mesoscale parameterization
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: ocean mesoscale eddy momentum fluxes / kinetic energy backscatter
code_availability: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12682335; original NW2 config via https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6993951
testbed_rationale: Provides open data and code for idealized Double Gyre and NeverWorld2 (NW2) MOM6 setups designed specifically for testing, benchmarking, and evaluating mesoscale eddy parameterizations online and offline across multiple resolutions.
pain_points: Grid-scale numerical instabilities and noise generation when implementing discovered closure online, requiring low-pass filtering passes and high-pass filtering of inputs.
Aliasing errors on Arakawa C-grid requiring a shift from energy-conserving to non-conserving discretization in NW2.
Very thin isopycnal layers (down to 10^-2 m) causing runtime crashes, negative thickness, or NaNs in multi-layer primitive equation setups.
Need for an ad-hoc attenuation function in regions of geostrophically unbalanced flows or high strain.
Filtering schemes increase online runtime overhead by 4-6% and cannot completely replace viscous/enstrophy dissipation, still requiring supplementary biharmonic Smagorinsky viscosity.
Trade-off between optimizing mean state (SSH, APE) and energizing eddies/reproducing backscatter (KE).
extraction_notes: The ZB20 equation was discovered in Zanna & Bolton (2020) using sparse regression / equation discovery; GZ21 is a CNN baseline evaluated in this work.
